name: sagittarius-scheme
desc: Free Scheme implementation supporting R6RS and R7RS
why: A capable R6RS and R7RS Scheme with a lot of standards coverage, an unusual and obscure implementation worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: Sagittarius Scheme is a Scheme implementation that the README describes as supporting the R6RS and R7RS specifications. Its runtime is written in C (the README says the C compiler must support C11). The Homebrew formula installs six executables: sagittarius, sash, compile-r7rs, compile-sagittarius, sagittarius-config and sagittarius-package. The README says the REPL was renamed to sagittarius in 0.5.6, with sash kept as a symbolic link. The README does not say what the compile-* and package tools do; their purposes below are guessed from their names only. The README does not describe what the language is used for or give a feature list.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no stated motivation. It only says it is a Scheme implementation supporting R6RS and R7RS. The scout notes call it capable with broad standards coverage, but that is not from the README.
brief.how_it_works: The README covers only the build. It uses CMake (minimum 3.12) and needs Boehm GC, zlib, libffi and OpenSSL. The README does not explain the runtime architecture or how Scheme code is executed.

brief.install_notes: Building from source needs CMake 3.12 or later and a C11 compiler, plus the libraries Boehm GC (threads enabled, pthreads), zlib, libffi and OpenSSL. CMake can download and build Boehm GC if you do not have it. On FreeBSD you need the threaded GC build (gc-threaded). On Windows the README uses MSVC (Visual Studio 2019 or later), NMake or Ninja, and Inno Setup for an installer. The Homebrew formula is the only route the README calls tested on macOS. For a 64-bit lib directory you can pass -DLIB_DIR=lib64. You may need to run ldconfig after install on Linux.
brief.standout: The README lists a support matrix with CI-tested and locally tested platforms and a Docker image for Linux ARM. It also keeps the legacy sash name as a symlink, which is a small detail of the project's history. Beyond that, the README does not show what sets it apart from other Schemes.
brief.status: unknown. The README has CI badges (GitHub Actions and CircleCI) and a 0.5.6 version reference, but I saw no release date, last-commit date or maintenance note. I did not fetch the repository's commit or release pages.
brief.caveats: Building from source takes several dependencies, and the README lists per-OS quirks (FreeBSD needs threaded GC; macOS may need CC and CXX set to GCC; the README advises a 32-bit build only for special cases). Windows needs Visual Studio and Inno Setup for the installer. The README points to a Google group for questions and to GitHub issues for bugs. The README does not state a license.
quotes: This is a Scheme implementation, supporting R6RS and R7RS specification.
Since 0.5.6, Sagittarius's REPL is renamed to `sagittarius` and legacy `sash` is kept as a symbolic link.
